title: Infection Spread Simulation II — Static Immunity
prompt:
This standalone problem is the second exercise in the Infection Spread Simulation series. Use `HEALTHY = 0`, `INFECTED = 1`, and `IMMUNE = 2`.

Implement `simulate_with_immunity(grid, infection_threshold=2, directions=DIR4)`. Propagation is synchronous: every daily transition reads the same start-of-day grid. A healthy cell becomes infected when it has at least `infection_threshold` infected neighbors. Infected cells remain infected. Immune cells never change and do not transmit.

Return `(days_to_stability, final_grid)`. Count a day only when at least one cell changes. You may assume the grid is non-empty and rectangular, every cell is a known state, and `infection_threshold` is a positive integer; you do not need to validate these inputs. Do not mutate the input. You do not need to implement Part I.
